title: Swerve Ball a multiplayer clone of the old Curve Ball flashgame
author: abesgarbo
selftext:
I recreated the old Curve Ball flash game as a multiplayer game with Claude. I've had the idea since I was a kid playing the original but never had the coding skills. It's the first real thing I've made with AI, and it took about a month on a Max plan.

Before giving anything to Claude Code, I used a Claude chat to make a step-by-step plan. That worked out pretty well, but getting the game to feel good was a lot of hands-on tuning.

I had CC build a harness so it could play the game itself, which mostly helped with tuning the bot difficulty levels. It could also take screenshots and see the changes it made, which helped a lot with the UI. I used the Google Stitch MCP to get the overall website aesthetic.

The netcode was a pain. When the original plan was designed I started on the wrong architecture (rollback, when it should have been event-driven), and fell down a rabbit hole of Claude trying to fix something that could never work. It took a few days of what felt like brute-forcing ideas before I scrapped it.

My workflow was mostly making design choices and copy-pasting: Claude chat told me what to tell CC, and whatever CC did I fed back into the chat to verify. Often the chat would tell me CC had made a mistake. It's a lot of copy-pasting, but it seemed to lead to the fewest mistakes.

Overall the vibe coding was enjoyable and I hope you guys enjoy the game! It plays best with a mouse, but I made it work on mobile too.

Question for you guys is what workflow works for you? Are you guys all just copy pasting back and forth too? I'd imagine in the future I can become something more than a messenger between Claude chat and CC
